warnings: Multiple experimental locations (greenhouse vs field) with different designs and sample sizes
Field experiments conducted in both dry and wet seasons - separate data points
Both tomato and sweet pepper tested - creates multiple species comparisons
Multiple pathogens tested (bacterial spot and early blight) - focus only on yield data
Integrated treatment (AN+F) alternates seaweed extract with fungicide - this is NOT a pure biostimulant treatment
Greenhouse experiments use n=30 plants per treatment, field experiments use n=200 plants per replicate with 3 replicates
Sample size confusion: field experiments have 3 replicates of 200 plants each, not n=200

recon.variance_source: Values are means ±SD of %disease indices on 45days after infection. Different letters denote significant differences at 95%confidence levels according to Fisher's protected LSD.
recon.control_definition: Water spray control (untreated control plants sprayed with water)
recon.treatment_definition: A.nodosum extract (AN) - 0.5% foliar spray applied every 10 days
recon.potential_tc_confusion: Fungicide treatments (F) and integrated treatments (AN+F) are also present - only extract AN vs Control for pure biostimulant effect
recon.sample_size_source: The experimental plots were arranged in a completely randomized design with three replicates and 200plants per replicate
recon.extraction_guidance: Extract only from Table 6 for fruit yield data. Compare AN (seaweed extract) vs Control treatments only. Do NOT use AN+F (integrated) treatment as this includes fungicide. Extract separate data points for: tomato dry season, tomato wet season, pepper dry season, pepper wet season. Use n=3 for field data. Greenhouse data lacks clear replication structure - use with caution if needed.
